title: The nuclear atom
summary: Atoms have a tiny dense nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons. Use atomic and mass numbers, explain isotopes and calculate relative atomic mass; at HL, interpret mass spectra.

keyterms.definition: The tiny, dense, positively charged centre of an atom containing protons and neutrons (nucleons) and almost all its mass.
Subatomic particle in the nucleus with relative mass 1 and relative charge +1.
Subatomic particle in the nucleus with relative mass 1 and no charge.
Subatomic particle outside the nucleus with relative charge −1 and a relative mass of about 1/1836 (≈ 0.0005).
The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom; it defines the element.
The total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus of an atom.
Atoms of the same element (same Z) with different numbers of neutrons, so different mass numbers.
The weighted mean mass of an atom of an element, relative to one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
A charged particle formed when an atom or group of atoms loses or gains electrons.
The percentage (or fraction) of atoms of an element that are a particular isotope.
Instrument that ionizes a sample and separates the ions by mass-to-charge ratio, giving isotopic masses and abundances.
The horizontal axis of a mass spectrum; for singly charged ions it equals the mass of the ion.

questions.prompt: How many neutrons are in an atom of ⁵⁶Fe (Z = 26)?
questions.explanation: Neutrons = A − Z = 56 − 26 = 30.

questions.statement: Almost all the mass of an atom is in its nucleus.
questions.explanation: Protons and neutrons each have relative mass 1, while electrons are about 1/1836 of that.

questions.prompt: Match each particle to its properties.
questions.explanation: These relative values are given in the data booklet and must be known.

questions.prompt: How many electrons are in the ion ³²S²⁻ (Z = 16)?
questions.explanation: A 2− charge means two extra electrons: 16 + 2 = 18.

questions.text: The number of protons in an atom is its ___ number.
questions.explanation: Atomic number Z = number of protons; it fixes the identity of the element.

questions.prompt: A species has 20 protons, 20 neutrons and 18 electrons. What is it?
questions.explanation: 20 protons = calcium; A = 20 + 20 = 40; two fewer electrons than protons gives a 2+ charge.

questions.statement: The nucleus occupies most of the volume of an atom.
questions.explanation: The nucleus is tiny (about 10⁻¹⁵ m across) compared with the atom (about 10⁻¹⁰ m); the atom is mostly empty space.

questions.text: The mass number of an atom with 17 protons and 20 neutrons is ___.
questions.explanation: A = protons + neutrons = 17 + 20 = 37 (this is chlorine-37).

questions.prompt: Which pair has the same number of electrons?
questions.explanation: Na⁺ has 11 − 1 = 10 electrons, the same as neon. They are isoelectronic.
Electron ≪ proton (1) < deuterium nucleus (2) < helium nucleus (4).

questions.prompt: Isotopes of an element have the same…
questions.explanation: Same number of protons and electrons, so the same electron configuration and chemistry. Different masses give slightly different physical properties (e.g. density, rate of diffusion).

questions.text: Chlorine is 75 % ³⁵Cl and 25 % ³⁷Cl. Its relative atomic mass is ___.

questions.statement: Relative atomic mass has no units.
questions.explanation: It is a ratio relative to 1/12 of a ¹²C atom, so it is dimensionless.

questions.prompt: Boron has isotopes ¹⁰B and ¹¹B and Ar = 10.8. What is the percentage abundance of ¹¹B?
questions.explanation: Let x = fraction of ¹¹B: 11x + 10(1 − x) = 10.8, so x = 0.8 → 80 %.

questions.statement: Isotopes of the same element have different physical properties such as density.
questions.explanation: Different numbers of neutrons change the mass, so density, boiling point and rate of diffusion differ slightly.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: Same Z, different number of neutrons
Weighted mean atomic mass relative to ¹²C/12

questions.explanation: Ar is an average over all isotopes, so it is usually not a whole number.

questions.prompt: Why is the Ar of copper (63.55) not a whole number?
options: Electrons add a large fractional mass
It is a weighted mean of isotopes ⁶³Cu and ⁶⁵Cu
questions.explanation: Ar averages the isotopes by abundance, so values lie between the isotope masses.

questions.text: Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons are called ___.
questions.explanation: Allotropes are different structural forms of an element (e.g. diamond and graphite); isotopes differ in neutrons.
Both have 6 protons but different neutron numbers. O₂ and O₃ are allotropes; the others are different elements.

questions.statement: An element with two isotopes in equal abundance has an Ar equal to the mean of the two isotopic masses.
questions.explanation: With 50 : 50 abundance the weighted mean is the simple mean.

questions.prompt: What does a mass spectrum of an element show?
questions.explanation: Each peak corresponds to an isotope (for 1+ ions); its height shows relative abundance.

questions.statement: For a singly charged ion, m/z equals the relative mass of the ion.
questions.explanation: With z = 1, m/z is just m.

questions.text: A mass spectrum shows peaks at m/z 24 (79 %), 25 (10 %) and 26 (11 %). The Ar is ___ (to 3 s.f.).

questions.prompt: A sample of bromine (⁷⁹Br and ⁸¹Br in roughly equal amounts) gives Br₂⁺ peaks. How many molecular-ion peaks appear?
questions.explanation: Combinations ⁷⁹Br⁷⁹Br (158), ⁷⁹Br⁸¹Br (160) and ⁸¹Br⁸¹Br (162) give three peaks in about 1 : 2 : 1 ratio.

questions.statement: The number of peaks in the mass spectrum of an element equals its number of isotopes (for 1+ ions).
questions.explanation: Each isotope gives one peak at its own m/z.

questions.prompt: Match the m/z of a singly charged ion to the isotope.
questions.explanation: For 1+ ions the m/z value is the mass number of the isotope.

questions.prompt: Lithium shows peaks at m/z 6 (7.5 %) and 7 (92.5 %). What is its Ar?

questions.text: In a mass spectrum, the height of each peak is proportional to the relative ___ of that isotope.
questions.explanation: Peak height (or area) gives how common each isotope is.

questions.prompt: Order the main stages in a mass spectrometer.
questions.explanation: The sample must be gaseous and ionized before ions can be accelerated, separated and detected.
